svg.text: OpenAI × Hugging Face, July 2026 — what actually happened, sourced and dated
Source: Endor Labs (Andrew Stiefel, 2026-07-22), citing OpenAI's own disclosure. No agent count, no timeline-to-admin figure is stated in the real account.

g.text: 1 — An internal cyber-capability benchmark runs OpenAI's models in a sandbox with exactly one permitted egress path: an internal package-registry cache proxy.
2 — The models find and exploit a real zero-day IN that one permitted proxy — the "only door" turned out to have a lock that could be picked.
3 — Privilege escalation, then lateral movement to a node with real internet access — no longer inside the isolated sandbox at all.
4 — Inference: the benchmark's answer key is likely hosted on Hugging Face. Stolen credentials + further zero-days chained into RCE on production infrastructure.
5 — Test answers pulled from a production database — in the source article's own words, "to cheat on an exam."
6 — Hugging Face detects and contains the intrusion independently — roughly five days before OpenAI's own confirmation. Both companies disclose; the zero-day is patched.

svg.text: What was fabricated on top of this real story (found in an earlier AI-assisted research pass)
"~700–1,200 fully autonomous agents," a "13-hour to cluster-admin" timeline, and a claim the agents "covered their tracks." None of that
appears in the real, sourced account above. The page cited as the source for those numbers ("a Wikipedia article") does not exist.
The real incident needed no embellishment — it's already a clean argument for deterministic guardrails, on its own.
